ASSISTANT: Congratulations on your new home! I'm Tom from Allstate. I'll help you get the right coverage. What's the address of your new home?
USER: It's 2847 Maple Drive in Naperville, Illinois, 60540.
ASSISTANT: Beautiful area! Tell me about the house - when was it built?
USER: It was built in 1998. It's a two-story colonial.
ASSISTANT: How many square feet?
USER: About 3,200 square feet, four bedrooms, three and a half baths.
ASSISTANT: Sounds lovely. What did you pay for it, if you don't mind me asking?
USER: We paid $485,000.
ASSISTANT: And when is your closing date?
USER: We close on September 20th, so next week.
ASSISTANT: Perfect timing. Is this your primary residence?
USER: Yes, we're moving from our condo in Chicago.
ASSISTANT: Great. Tell me about the roof - what type and how old?
USER: It's architectural shingles, replaced in 2019.
ASSISTANT: That's good, relatively new. What about the heating and cooling systems?
USER: Forced air heating and central AC. The furnace is from 2018, AC from 2020.
ASSISTANT: Excellent, updated systems. Any fireplace?
USER: Yes, a gas fireplace in the family room.
ASSISTANT: Is there a basement?
USER: Yes, full finished basement with a rec room and office.
ASSISTANT: Is it a walkout basement?
USER: No, just regular basement with small windows.
ASSISTANT: Got it. Any pool or hot tub?
USER: No pool, but there's a hot tub on the back deck that we're keeping.
ASSISTANT: We'll need to note that for liability. How old is the hot tub?
USER: The sellers said it's about 3 years old, a 6-person tub.
ASSISTANT: Is the deck attached to the house?
USER: Yes, it's a large wood deck, probably 20 by 15 feet.
ASSISTANT: Any other structures on the property? Shed, detached garage?
USER: There's a shed in the backyard, maybe 10 by 12.
ASSISTANT: What about the attached garage?
USER: Oh yes, two-car attached garage.
ASSISTANT: Now, let me ask about claims history. Any claims on this property that you know of?
USER: The seller disclosed one claim for wind damage to the roof in 2017, which is why they replaced it in 2019.
ASSISTANT: Thanks for letting me know. Do you have any dogs?
USER: We have a golden retriever, very friendly.
ASSISTANT: Golden retrievers are fine. No breed restrictions for them. Any trampolines?
USER: No, but we're thinking of getting a swing set for the kids.
ASSISTANT: Swing sets are fine. Now, for coverage amounts. I'd recommend dwelling coverage of at least $380,000 for rebuild cost.
USER: Why not the full $485,000?
ASSISTANT: That's your purchase price including land. We insure the structure replacement cost. Land doesn't burn down. $380,000 should fully rebuild your home.
USER: That makes sense.
ASSISTANT: For personal property, I suggest $285,000, which is 75% of dwelling coverage.
USER: Is that enough? We have some nice furniture and electronics.
ASSISTANT: It should be, but do you have any high-value items? Jewelry, art, collectibles?
USER: My wife has an engagement ring worth about $12,000.
ASSISTANT: Standard policies limit jewelry to $2,500. You'd want a rider for the ring. It's about $120 per year for $12,000 coverage.
USER: Yes, let's add that.
ASSISTANT: Good choice. For liability, I recommend $500,000, especially with the hot tub.
USER: What does that cover?
ASSISTANT: If someone gets injured on your property and sues. Hot tubs increase risk.
USER: Makes sense. What about deductibles?
ASSISTANT: Standard is $1,000, but you can go to $2,500 to save on premium.
USER: What's the savings?
ASSISTANT: With $1,000 deductible, your annual premium is $1,847. With $2,500, it's $1,592.
USER: Let's do the $1,000 deductible. I don't want a big out-of-pocket if something happens.
ASSISTANT: Understood. Do you want water backup coverage? It covers sewer or drain backups.
USER: Is that common in Naperville?
ASSISTANT: We see claims occasionally, especially with older homes. It's $75 per year for $10,000 coverage.
USER: Yes, add it. Better safe than sorry.
ASSISTANT: Smart. Your total annual premium is $2,042. Would you like to pay in full or monthly?
USER: What's the difference?
ASSISTANT: Paid in full saves you $84. Monthly is $178 for 12 months.
USER: I'll pay in full.
ASSISTANT: Excellent. Your policy number will be HO-558847291.
USER: And this starts September 20th?
ASSISTANT: Yes, effective 12:01 AM on September 20th. I'll email the binder for your closing.
USER: Perfect, my email is danielpark85@email.com
ASSISTANT: Got it. Oh, what's your full name for the policy?
USER: Daniel and Sarah Park.
ASSISTANT: Thank you. I'm sending the insurance binder now. Your mortgage company will need this.
USER: It's First National Bank, should I have them contact you?
ASSISTANT: I'll need their information to list them as mortgagee.
USER: I have it here... First National Bank, loan number 445872291.
ASSISTANT: Perfect. They're listed on the policy. Now, let me ask about your current condo - do you have insurance on that?
USER: Yes, through State Farm, but we're canceling once we move.
ASSISTANT: Make sure to time that cancellation right. You want overlap, not a gap.
USER: Good point. When should I cancel?
ASSISTANT: Once you've completely moved out and handed over the keys. Maybe end of September?
USER: That sounds right. Oh, what about flood insurance?
ASSISTANT: Your property is in Zone X - minimal flood risk. Not required by your lender.
USER: Should I get it anyway?
ASSISTANT: For Zone X, it's about $450 per year. It's peace of mind, but statistically very low risk.
USER: I'll skip it for now. What about an umbrella policy?
ASSISTANT: With your home value and hot tub, I'd recommend it. $1 million umbrella is about $200 per year.
USER: What does that cover?
ASSISTANT: Liability beyond your home and auto limits. Protects your assets if you're sued.
USER: Let me think about that. Can I add it later?
ASSISTANT: Absolutely. Just call us when you're ready.
USER: What about home warranty? The seller offered to pay for one year.
ASSISTANT: That's different from insurance. Home warranty covers appliance and system repairs.
USER: Oh right, that's through American Home Shield.
ASSISTANT: Good company. That covers what insurance doesn't - wear and tear issues.
USER: Speaking of wear and tear, what if my roof needs replacement in 10 years?
ASSISTANT: Normal aging isn't covered. But if a storm damages it, we'd cover replacement minus depreciation.
USER: How does depreciation work?
ASSISTANT: For roofs, we depreciate about 5% per year after 10 years old. Your roof is 5 years old, so full replacement value now.

USER: It's a three-flat building. I'll live in one unit and rent the other two.

USER: 1925, but it's been renovated.

ASSISTANT: Great updates. What about the roof?
USER: Flat rubber roof, replaced in 2018.

USER: Each unit is about 1,100 square feet, so 3,300 total.

USER: I paid $675,000.

USER: The first floor unit.
ASSISTANT: Are the other units currently rented?

ASSISTANT: What's the rent for the second floor?
USER: They pay $1,850 per month.
ASSISTANT: Good rental income. What will you charge for the third floor?
USER: Probably $2,000 after renovation.
ASSISTANT: Do you have a lease with the current tenant?
USER: Yes, they have 8 months left on their lease.
ASSISTANT: Good. For owner-occupied multi-family, we need different coverage. You need a homeowners policy for your unit and landlord coverage for the rentals.
USER: That's confusing. I thought one policy would cover everything.
ASSISTANT: It's actually one policy but with different coverage sections. Your unit gets full homeowners coverage, rental units get dwelling and liability.
USER: Oh wait, I already have homeowners insurance on my house in Naperville.
ASSISTANT: That's fine, this is separate. Are you Daniel Park?
USER: Yes! You helped me with my Naperville house last month!
ASSISTANT: Oh, I thought the name sounded familiar! Policy HO-558847291, right?
USER: That's right.
ASSISTANT: Great, we can bundle these for additional savings. So this Chicago property is an investment?
USER: Well, we're actually planning to move into it eventually.
ASSISTANT: When are you planning to move?
USER: Maybe in a year or two. My wife wants to be back in the city.
ASSISTANT: That changes things. Will you keep the Naperville house?
USER: We might rent it out then.
ASSISTANT: Interesting flip! Well, for now, let's set up the Chicago property correctly.
USER: Yes, I need insurance ASAP. I close tomorrow.
ASSISTANT: Tomorrow! We can do that. Let me get the details. Each unit has its own entrance?
USER: Yes, separate entrances and utilities.
ASSISTANT: That's good for insurance. What about parking?
USER: Two-car garage in back, plus one spot in the driveway.
ASSISTANT: Who gets the parking?
USER: Each unit gets one spot.
ASSISTANT: Fair setup. Any common areas?
USER: Shared basement for laundry and storage.
ASSISTANT: Is the basement finished?
USER: No, just concrete floors and walls.
ASSISTANT: Any flooding history?
USER: The seller said no issues, but it's near the lake so I'm concerned.
ASSISTANT: You're not in a flood zone, but water backup coverage is smart. For dwelling coverage, I recommend $520,000.
USER: For the whole building?
ASSISTANT: Yes, that should cover rebuild costs for the structure.
USER: What about my stuff versus tenant stuff?
ASSISTANT: Your personal property in your unit is covered. Tenants need their own renters insurance for their belongings.
USER: Do I require that?
ASSISTANT: I highly recommend requiring it. Protects both you and them.
USER: I'll add that to the lease. What about liability?
ASSISTANT: For a rental, I suggest $1 million liability minimum.
USER: That seems high.
ASSISTANT: Tenants and guests can sue if injured. Stairs in a three-flat are a common claim area.
USER: Good point. The stairs are old wood, actually.
ASSISTANT: Might want to add grip strips. Also, what about loss of rent coverage?
USER: What's that?
ASSISTANT: If damage makes units unrentable, we cover lost rental income. Important for your cash flow.
USER: Yes, definitely need that. How much?
ASSISTANT: Based on your rents, I'd suggest $30,000 coverage, about 12 months of income.
USER: Perfect. What about this renovation I'm doing?
ASSISTANT: You should notify us when renovation is complete. Vacant units have different risk.
USER: The third floor should be done in two months.
ASSISTANT: Good. We'll note it's under renovation. Any other improvements planned?
USER: Eventually I want to add central air. The building only has window units now.
ASSISTANT: That would increase value and reduce risk. Window units can cause water damage.
USER: True. What's the premium for all this?
ASSISTANT: For this property, annual premium is $3,247.
USER: That's more than my house!
ASSISTANT: Rental properties have higher risk. But with your multi-policy discount, it's $2,922.
USER: That's better. Can I pay monthly?
ASSISTANT: You can, but you save 8% paying annually - that's $234.
USER: I'll pay annually then. Same credit card?
ASSISTANT: I can use the same card on file if you'd like.
USER: Yes, that works.
ASSISTANT: Perfect. Your Chicago property policy number is HO-558897435.
USER: I need the binder for tomorrow's closing.
ASSISTANT: I'm emailing it now to danielpark85@email.com.
USER: Great. What about inspections?
ASSISTANT: We may do an exterior inspection in the first 60 days, just to verify information.
USER: Will you go inside?
ASSISTANT: Not usually, unless we see concerns outside. We'll notify you first.
USER: Good. So now I have two properties insured with you.
ASSISTANT: Yes, your primary residence in Naperville and your rental in Chicago. Both fully covered!
USER: What if I have questions about claims or coverage?
ASSISTANT: Call our 24/7 line, or use the mobile app. Your agent is also available during business hours.
USER: Who is my agent?
ASSISTANT: Jim Patterson is your local agent. His office is in downtown Naperville.
USER: Oh good, that's convenient.
ASSISTANT: He can help with any policy changes or questions. I'll copy him on your new policy.
USER: Perfect. Thanks Michelle, you've been very helpful!
ASSISTANT: You're welcome! Good luck with your rental property, Mr. Park!
